properties.title: Representing Uncertainty in Property Valuation Through a Bayesian Deep Learning Approach
properties.healthcare_scope: absent for the implemented and evaluated task
properties.membership_rationale: Both evaluated methods are static property-price regressors, without a persistent evolving world state or a successor-state transition. Healthcare appears as motivation, proposed applicability and cited literature.
properties.generic_relevance: Bayesian predictive uncertainty and the distinction between uncertainty characterization, calibration and validated selective prediction.
properties.author_priority_claim: First Bayesian deep-neural-network study of property-valuation uncertainty; not independently verified.

properties.supplements: No separate supplements supplied; no appendix identified in the nine-page article.

properties.version_boundary: Paper-described configuration; trained artifact, run identifier and fitted variational parameters not reported.

properties.world_coordinate: None. Parameter optimization and repeated predictive draws are not world transitions.

properties.scope: Executed offline prediction and uncertainty-analysis workflow
properties.flow: Tabular preprocessing → separate ANN and BNN predictions → held-out price-error comparison; BNN dispersion compared with ANN residuals and displayed geographically.

properties.encoding_consultation: KAPA valuation manuals and two field appraisers informed conversion; this is not model-output evaluation.

properties.uncertainty_analysis: BNN predictive range and standard deviation versus ANN residuals; geographic dispersion map.
properties.architecture_selection: Best in most trials asserted; selection protocol not reported.

properties.boundary: No measured predictive coverage, selective-risk acceptance, post-filter error or referral benefit is reported.

properties.purpose: Offline research on property-price prediction and uncertainty
properties.action_execution: No modeled or executed environmental action in the reported experiment.

evidence_fragments.source_ref: Papers/065_2020_Representing Uncertainty in Property Valuation Through a Bayesian Deep Learning Approach.pdf
evidence_fragments.content:
Uncertainty in predictions that arise from the uncertainty in weights is called epistemic uncertainty 
(Kendall & Gal, 2017). This kind of uncertainty can be reduced if we obtain enough data. Thus, 
epistemic uncertainty would be higher in regions of little training data, and lower in regions of 
abundant training data in proper ty valuation tasks. Uncertainty co ming from the inherent noise in 
training data is an example of aleatoric uncertainty. It cannot be reduced even if  more training data is 
given. Aleatoric uncertainty is covered by the probability distribution used to define the likelihood 
function, and we do not discuss this uncertainty in the present study.

scope.R4: Appraisers advised preprocessing, not a reported reader/use evaluation of model outputs.

gate_assessments.rationale: Provenance is incomplete and training-only preprocessing, repeated-property overlap and model-selection/test separation are unestablished. No leakage failure is demonstrated.
The scoped method is static regression, not a claimed temporal world model. Static price MSE is not successor-state evidence.
No multitime forecast or rollout is intended in the executed configuration.
The proposed decision depends on uncertainty, but calibration and accepted tolerance evidence are not reported. Dispersion cutoffs and regression-line confidence bands cannot satisfy this gate.
No action-conditioned or alternative-action prediction is queried.
No prediction is interpreted as an identified intervention effect or therapeutic benefit.
No world-model-coupled planner or learned action policy exists in the assessed implementation.
For the proposed high-stakes financial use, operational blocking, abstention, fallback and referral effectiveness are unestablished. This is not evidence that an executed guard failed.
Claims of wider real-world usefulness and possible reuse beyond the sampled transactions lack external, subgroup or composition-transfer evidence. This is not a demonstrated transfer-test failure.
The scoped empirical component study does not evaluate human usability or sim-to-real utility. Proposed inspection is not a completed human-use claim.
No live clinical workflow or patient-benefit use is studied.
This assessment concerns an offline research comparison, not an operational release dossier. Potential financial deployment remains a proposal, and no authorization is inferred.

legacy_cells.B: Representing Uncertainty in Property Valuation Through a Bayesian Deep Learning Approach
legacy_cells.I: 065_2020_Representing Uncertainty in Property Valuation Through a Bayesian Deep Learning Approach.pdf
legacy_cells.FX: Read the complete extracted PDF text (all 9 PDF pages). Relevant sections inspected: title/byline/abstract (p. 1); introduction and literature review (pp. 1–3); data, cohort and network architecture (pp. 3–5); results and Table 3 (p. 6); uncertainty analysis and Figs. 3–4 (pp. 7–8); conclusions and limitations (p. 8); remaining references (p. 9). Tables 1–3 and figure captions/descriptions were inspected. | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: The paper evaluates static real-estate price prediction and uncertainty estimation, not a healthcare task; its methods/results do not demonstrate a health-state temporal transition. Exclusion is based on the paper itself, not metadata or prior screening notes. Table 1 text layout is imperfectly extracted; no values from that table were used. A:I were left untouched. Evidence QA: 6/6 populated fields had a <=25-word quotation matching extracted PDF text (100%). Confidence is conservative; review this row where exact quote checks were incomplete. Codex audit: 6 prior populated fields have a located source quotation; 0 have quotations not located by normalized text matching. Unlocated quotations are review flags, not proof that the value is false. Companion evidence audit lists affected columns. Reviewer FS/FT/FU mappings are synthesis. Prior unsupported/missing fields remain Not reported; no clinical benefit inferred from offline simulation.

limitations: This is automated model review, not independent human verification, independent replication or clinical validation.

The current synthesis read every supplied text page, image-review note and operational feature definition, but received no page-image pixels. Earlier documented API page calls received and reported reviewing every page image and text; this provenance is preserved separately.

Several page notes contain stale chunk-local statements that other pages were unavailable. They do not negate assembled nine-page coverage and must not be used as the current availability description.
Source hash, page count, source path and earlier request receipts are supplied provenance, not independently recomputed or checked in this synthesis.
No filesystem access, external bibliography or repository inspection, executable schema validation, graph rebuild or project-file write was performed.
Bibliographic details are supported by supplied title-page material. Peer-review status and novelty claims were not independently checked.

Both models are static nonclinical regressors. Generic feature-adapter, task-readout and uncertainty assertions do not establish complete blueprint modules, healthcare reuse or world-model membership.
No clinical readiness facet is assigned. Property records are not actual human/clinical validation data, and appraiser encoding consultation is not R4 output evaluation.
Acquisition source, release identifier, detailed sampling, missingness, repeated-property identities and asset access terms are insufficiently reported.
Training-only standardization and maximum-price normalization, architecture-selection separation and random-split independence are not established. Leakage is possible but not demonstrated.
Spatial clustering, potential repeated transactions and a partial-ownership observation limit simple independent whole-property interpretations.
Intermediate categories are omitted from several ordinal mappings. Alternative encoding sensitivity and the imposed ordering/spacing assumptions are not evaluated.
Exact priors, likelihood, variational family, activations, optimizer, training duration, seeds and convergence diagnostics are insufficiently specified; cited systems' details are not inherited.

Equation (2) has an apparent supervised-data evidence-integral notation problem in the supplied text and earlier image review. Its implementation implications remain unknown; it is not silently repaired.
BNN MSE aggregation is ambiguous. The reported 0.008 and 0.016 are retained without derived ratios, invented significance or confidence intervals.
ANN residuals require observed prices and are not independently observed uncertainty truth. The transformation producing nonnegative plotted residuals is insufficiently defined.

Maximum-normalized targets, the illustrative range 0.3 and reported screening thresholds 6.0 and 0.75 are retained. Their scale relationship is unresolved; unbounded Bayesian predictions mean normalization alone does not prove an impossibility.
Figure 3's 95% band is for the fitted regression line, not individual predictive intervals or calibrated coverage.

Earlier image notes describe substantial scatter and large errors below proposed cutoffs. These are attributed to earlier automated visual review, not new pixel inspection or a quantified selective-risk experiment.
Geographic uncertainty patterns do not isolate causal effects of training density or property rarity and do not establish validated OOD detection.
Aleatoric uncertainty is explicitly outside the reported analysis. This supports absence of separate two-component estimation, not absence of every likelihood-noise contribution.
No independent threshold-selection set, retention rate, rejection fraction, post-filter error, referral outcome or measured operational benefit supports the screening proposal.
The relationship between the two cutoffs, equality handling, human availability and fallback behavior are unresolved.
Algorithm choice, convergence and priors are suggested explanations for BNN underperformance, not experimentally isolated causes.
The authors' real-world valuation suitability and broader medical applicability claims exceed the demonstrated offline evidence.
References on pages 8–9 were reviewed as citations, not retrieved studies; their methods, clinical data and capabilities are not attributed to this work.
Raw legacy cells are preserved, including inaccurate historical locators and earlier extraction claims. Preservation does not endorse their correctness.
No evidence gate is passed, clinical threshold invented, release authorized or validated composition inferred.
notes: Physical PDF pages are authoritative; printed pages are 15–23. Shared system assertions cover both paper-described regressors where their mechanisms and dispositions coincide. Model-specific uncertainty assertions and a separate proposed-screening context preserve necessary differences. All 128 operational feature IDs are represented; repetitive identical per-model assertions have been consolidated without discarding distinct dispositions. Full operational definitions were supplied and considered in this review, superseding earlier claims that they were unavailable. The erroneous statements that assertions were empty or requested to be empty have been removed.
